subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Mixture and Alligation — Ratios, Concentrations and Blending (W10 B2)

questions.stem: In what ratio must a grocer mix rice costing ₹30/kg and ₹40/kg to get a mixture worth ₹36/kg?
questions.explanation: B is correct. By alligation: cheap variety (₹30) part = (40−36) = 4; expensive variety (₹40) part = (36−30) = 6. Ratio = 4:6 = 2:3. Verify: (2×30+3×40)/(2+3) = (60+120)/5 = 180/5 = 36 ✓. Trap: 1:2 uses wrong differences; 3:4 misapplies the alligation cross.

questions.stem: In what ratio must milk (at ₹20/L) and water (at ₹0/L) be mixed to obtain a mixture worth ₹12/L?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Water part = (20−12) = 8; Milk part = (12−0) = 12. Ratio (milk:water) = 12:8 = 3:2. Verify: (3×20+2×0)/5 = 60/5 = ₹12 ✓. Trap: 2:3 reverses milk and water; 3:5 miscomputes the alligation cross.

questions.stem: A 60-litre mixture of milk and water contains 80% milk. How many litres of water must be added to make the milk percentage 60%?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Milk = 80% of 60 = 48 L. Let x L water be added. 48/(60+x) = 0.60. 60+x = 80. x = 20 L. Verify: 48/80 = 0.60 = 60% ✓. Trap: 15 L solves 48/(60+x)=0.64; 24 L gives 48/84≈57% (not 60%).

questions.stem: Two alloys contain gold and silver in ratios 2:3 and 3:2 respectively. In what ratio should they be mixed so that the resulting alloy has equal quantities of gold and silver?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Alloy A: gold fraction = 2/5. Alloy B: gold fraction = 3/5. Target = 1/2. Alligation on gold: Alloy A part = |3/5−1/2| = 1/10; Alloy B part = |1/2−2/5| = 1/10. Ratio = 1:1. Verify: (1×2/5+1×3/5)/2 = (2/5+3/5)/2 = 1/2 ✓. Equal mixing gives equal gold and silver.

questions.stem: A 40-litre mixture of acid and water contains 20% acid. How much water must be added to make the acid percentage 10%?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Acid = 20% of 40 = 8 L. Let x L water added. 8/(40+x) = 0.10. 40+x = 80. x = 40 L. Verify: 8/80 = 0.10 = 10% ✓. Trap: 30 L gives 8/70 ≈ 11.4% (not 10%); 35 L gives 8/75 ≈ 10.7%.

questions.stem: Three varieties of tea at ₹60, ₹90, and ₹120 per kg are mixed in ratio 2:3:1. Find the cost of the resulting blend per kg.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Weighted average = (2×60+3×90+1×120)/(2+3+1) = (120+270+120)/6 = 510/6 = ₹85/kg. Trap: ₹90 = simple average (60+90+120)/3 (ignores the weights/ratios); ₹80 = (2×60+3×80+1×60)/6 (wrong prices).

questions.stem: A merchant mixes two brands of coffee worth ₹40/kg and ₹60/kg in ratio 2:3. He sells 25 kg of the blend at ₹60/kg. Find his profit.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Blend cost per kg = (2×40+3×60)/5 = (80+180)/5 = ₹52/kg. CP of 25 kg = 25×52 = ₹1,300. SP = 25×60 = ₹1,500. Profit = 1500−1300 = ₹200. Trap: ₹250 uses wrong cost ₹50/kg (equal-weight average instead of ratio-weighted); ₹300 ignores cost altogether.

questions.stem: A wine merchant wishes to make 75 litres of wine of 40% purity by mixing two wines of 30% and 45% purity. How many litres of the 45% wine should be used?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Alligation: 30% wine part = (45−40) = 5; 45% wine part = (40−30) = 10. Ratio of 30%:45% = 5:10 = 1:2. Total 3 parts = 75 L → 1 part = 25 L. 30% wine = 25 L, 45% wine = 50 L. Verify: 25×0.30+50×0.45 = 7.5+22.5 = 30 L pure. 30/75 = 0.40 = 40% ✓. Trap: 25 L is the 30% wine quantity (not the 45%).

questions.stem: In what ratio must two varieties of salt at ₹6/kg and ₹8/kg be mixed so that by selling the mixture at ₹8.25/kg, there is a gain of 10%?
questions.explanation: C is correct. SP = ₹8.25 at 10% profit → CP of blend = 8.25/1.10 = ₹7.50/kg. Alligation on ₹6 and ₹8 to get mean ₹7.50: ₹6 variety part = (8−7.5) = 0.5; ₹8 variety part = (7.5−6) = 1.5. Ratio = 0.5:1.5 = 1:3 (cheaper:dearer). Trap: 3:1 reverses the two varieties; 2:1 uses wrong values.

questions.stem: A 20-litre vessel contains a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3:1. How much of the mixture should be replaced with pure milk so that the ratio becomes 4:1?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Current: milk=15L, water=5L. Let x L mixture be replaced with x L milk. Water remaining = 5×(1−x/20) = 5−x/4. Total = 20. Milk = 20 − (5−x/4) = 15+x/4. Ratio 4:1 → water = 20/5 = 4. 5−x/4 = 4 → x/4 = 1 → x = 4L. Verify: replace 4L (containing 3L milk+1L water) with 4L milk. Water=5−1=4. Milk=15−3+4=16. Ratio=16:4=4:1 ✓. Trap: 5L gives water=5−5/4=3.75 and milk=16.25, ratio≠4:1.
